name: regkv
description: Read a Windows registry hive with regipy: a key's values (each with its registry type and length, read whole: regipy's default cut to 256 characters is not taken), its subkeys with their last-written times (raw FILETIME and ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits), and a bounded recursive listing. A reader, not a decoder: a binary value comes back as hex and nothing more, so UserAssist, ShimCache, BAM, SAM and ShellBag values are not decoded here. Completeness is said: unreadable keys and values are under problems, branches the walk did not enter (depth or node limit, or an error) under stopped_branches, and the whole recursive listing is kept in a file the answer names past the inline page; status is complete or partial (partial when a problem was named, a branch was not entered or the inline listing was cut) and status_basis says which. Every key listed is also in a file the answer names (all_subkeys) when the inline list of 2,000 is not the whole of it. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive: a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values, so an index that repeats one list (an ri element named again and again) is read to that bound, listed once per key, and said under problems; it is not followed. The tool stops at its own time limit (27 seconds) with what it walked and names the branches it did not open; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file. Problems are a page (the first 50 inline, all in the file all_problems names); the names of a missing key's siblings are at most 200 (subkeys_there_count). A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. A value name that repeats is numbered once per name ('name (2)'). A big-endian DWORD is a problem (regipy returns no data for the type). The library's own messages, which can hold bytes of a value or a name, are counted (library_messages_withheld) and never printed. depth is 0 to 128; a key whose subkey list was already reached (a cycle, or a list two keys share) is named and not entered again; a key that declares more values than were read is a problem; a hive that is not a regular file (a named pipe) is not opened. hive_dirty (the two sequence numbers differ) and the transaction logs beside the hive are reported; the logs are NOT replayed, so a dirty hive's newest state may be missing. SENSITIVE: values whose name says password, secret, token or credential (a DWORD or QWORD excepted), every value under Policy\Secrets, PolEKList and PolSecretEncryptionKey of a SECURITY hive, the cached logons (NL$) and the V value of each SAM user are replaced by a marker holding only their length and listed under sensitive_values_withheld; the type of a value never lets one through, and the place is judged by the key names the hive holds, not by the spelling asked for. No flag brings one back. A secret inside a value that does not look like one (a command line with a password in it, an ImagePath) is NOT recognised and comes back whole. The key path is read from the hive's root, a leading backslash or not. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (key names, value names and value data): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text. A filter on content (contains) is applied to the text that is shown, never to what is withheld. write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on 1,000 random plants per shape and context (175 cells): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys, connection strings, user-info (also with an @ inside the password), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, case-folded and glued prefixes: none printed whole; AWS-shaped, 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys: at most 2.2% (letters-only keys with a slash); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters: at most 0.5%; random lower-case letters of 24: 9.4%; a 16-character base32 seed: 11%. Real Windows strings changed (any part withheld) in 9,950 generated registry, file, service, package and host names, SIDs, GUIDs and typed digests (2 changed: the 32-digit hash in a Chrome and an Edge autolaunch value name) and 3,431 strings of real event logs (25 changed: 17 of 1,040 whole event records, 7 of 313 command lines and messages, 1 of 322 path fields; they hold encoded PowerShell payloads and the 32-digit hash directories of the .NET native-image cache). NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits, anything under 16 characters in a name; 75% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

hive.description: Path to the registry hive file on disk (a copy; transaction logs beside it are named, not applied)

key.description: Registry key path, backslash form e.g. \Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion

depth.description: Levels below the key to open when recurse=true (default 2); a branch left closed is listed under stopped_branches

limit.description: Recursive nodes shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); the whole listing is in the file named by all_nodes

max_nodes.description: Upper bound on the nodes a recursive walk visits (default 1000000); branches left past it are listed under stopped_branches

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
